latest_apis.rationale: The whole app sits on the newest stable Qwik (1.20.3, released days before this review) and uses the current generation of its APIs end-to-end — routeLoader$ + resolveValue heads, status(404), signals instead of the v2-deprecated useResource$, callable useNavigate, current useVisibleTask$ signature — and avoids every v2-deprecated API. The single deduction is the home page hand-rolling history mutation and a popstate sync instead of the framework's navigation primitives (verified against qwik.dev docs and the v2 upgrade guide, next.qwik.dev/docs/upgrade/).

platform.rationale: It reaches for the platform first everywhere it matters — fetch with a promise-dedup cache, URL/URLSearchParams for all query handling, native form elements and semantic tables with aria-sort, CSS custom properties, lazy images — with zero polyfills and no hand-rolled widgets. The only nit (regex ID extraction at app/src/lib/api.ts:44 instead of the URL API) is too small to pull the score down.

dependencies.rationale: The runtime footprint is exactly what it should be — none — and the build tooling is modern, but the dev-side list carries three questionable picks: an unused undici, an unused typescript-plugin-css-modules on a floating 'latest' version, and a stale TypeScript/@types pin, plus an ESLint stack that has no config file and therefore never executes (including the valuable eslint-plugin-qwik rules).

churn_resistance.rationale: The architecture is genuinely upgrade-friendly: all data access is behind one typed module, routes are thin, config matches what the current CLI generates, and no framework internals or deprecated APIs are relied on (the v2 migration guide confirms nothing the app uses is removed). It loses a point for the home page's bespoke history-sync layer, the module-scope env read, and pervasive 'any' inside the otherwise well-typed boundary.

findings.issue: The 'lint' script targets eslint 9, which requires a flat config, but there is no eslint.config.* anywhere under app/ (verified by ls/grep) — so the declared eslint stack (eslint 9.32, eslint-plugin-qwik ^1.20.3, @eslint/js, typescript-eslint, globals) never runs and Qwik-specific lint rules that guard against resumability mistakes are not enforced.
findings.suggestion: Add the create-qwik eslint.config.mjs that wires eslint-plugin-qwik + typescript-eslint, so future edits are checked; otherwise remove the five unused lint packages.

findings.issue: Filter state is kept in four signals mirroring the URL and re-synced via a hand-rolled popstate listener, with five separate hand-rolled window.history.pushState/replaceState call sites (lines 69, 86, 108, 141, 158) that pass window.history.state along — a private, parallel routing layer that duplicates what Qwik City's router (useNavigate() / <Link replaceState>) owns and can silently desync from it.
findings.suggestion: Drive the URL through useNavigate()/Link (which support replace semantics and keep the router's state coherent), or derive the four control values from a single reactive read of location.url instead of mirroring them in signals.

findings.issue: API_BASE_URL is read from process.env at module scope, freezing it at process boot and coupling the data layer to Node process semantics rather than the request environment Qwik City exposes.
findings.suggestion: Read it per request via the request event's env API (event.env.get('API_BASE_URL')) passed down from the routeLoaders, or at minimum resolve it lazily inside fetchJson.

findings.issue: undici: "*" and typescript-plugin-css-modules: "latest" are unused starter leftovers (no undici import anywhere; the app writes plain CSS), and the floating version specifiers mean builds are not reproducible.
findings.suggestion: Remove both packages; if kept, pin exact versions.

findings.issue: typescript is pinned to 5.4.5 (a 2024 release) and @types/node to 20.19.0 while the app runs on Node 24 and the latest Chromium — stale pins inherited from an older starter.
findings.suggestion: Bump to the current TypeScript release and @types/node matching the Node 24 runtime.

findings.issue: Pokémon IDs are extracted from API URLs with a hand-rolled regex (/\/(\d+)\/?$/) instead of the platform's URL API.
findings.suggestion: Parse with new URL(url).pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean).pop() (or keep the regex but centralize it — it already is — this is a minor polish item).

findings.issue: The data layer is typed at its boundary but 'any' throughout its body (englishName(names: any[]), TypeInfo.detail: any, evolutionTree(node: any), entry: any in every find/map), and 'any' leaks into templates (app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:57,73) where typed data already exists.
findings.suggestion: Declare minimal interfaces for the PokeAPI payloads (Ref, NamedResource, FlavorEntry…) so the boundary types actually protect the routes.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache is created through a (globalThis as any).__pokedexApiCache ??= hack with a string magic key, an untyped global that invites collisions and hides the cache from the type system.
findings.suggestion: Use a typed module-scope Map (or a WeakMap keyed off the server entry) and let the bundler own module identity.

findings.issue: Dead export typeClassName is never used (grep: only its definition), and package.json still carries the starter's sharp-era 'engines-annotation' and placeholder 'deploy' script (app/package.json:6,14) despite the app doing no image optimization or adapter deploys.
findings.suggestion: Delete the dead export and the scaffold annotations that describe features the app doesn't use.

findings.issue: All internal links are plain <a> elements rather than Qwik City's <Link>, which adds data/symbol prefetching for client-side navigations (Qwik City still intercepts the clicks, so this is purely a lost optimization, not a bug).
findings.suggestion: Use <Link> for in-app hrefs to get prefetch behavior for free.

summary: This is a current-generation Qwik City app on the newest stable release (1.20.3, days old at review time), using routeLoader$ + resolveValue heads, signals, the callable useNavigate, and none of the APIs the imminent v2 deprecates — its config is verbatim current-scaffold, so framework upgrades stay cheap. Platform usage is exemplary (native fetch with a promise cache, URL/URLSearchParams, native form controls and tables, CSS custom properties) and all data access hides behind one typed module. The costs are maintenance-shaped: a hand-rolled history/popstate layer on the home page that bypasses the router, an ESLint stack with no config so linting never runs, unused floating devDeps (undici, typescript-plugin-css-modules), stale TypeScript pins, and 'any' leaking inside the otherwise well-typed data layer.
